# Forecast case and sequence notifications using variant of concern strain dynamics

> **Archived.** No longer maintained; last updated May 2023.

[![R-CMD-as-cran-check](https://github.com/epiforecasts/forecast.vocs/actions/workflows/R-CMD-as-cran-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/epiforecasts/forecast.vocs/actions/workflows/R-CMD-as-cran-check.yaml)
[![Codecov test
coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/epiforecasts/forecast.vocs/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/epiforecasts/forecast.vocs)

[![Universe](https://epiforecasts.r-universe.dev/badges/forecast.vocs)](https://epiforecasts.r-universe.dev/)
[![MIT
license](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](https://github.com/epiforecasts/forecast.vocs/blob/master/LICENSE.md/)
[![GitHub
contributors](https://img.shields.io/github/contributors/epiforecasts/forecast.vocs)](https://github.com/epiforecasts/forecast.vocs/graphs/contributors)

[![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/383161374.svg)](https://zenodo.org/badge/latestdoi/383161374)

Contains models and tools to produce short-term forecasts for both case
and sequence notifications assuming circulation of either one or two
variants. Tools are also provided to allow the evaluation of the use of
sequence data for short-term forecasts in both real-world settings and
in user generated scenarios.

## Installation

### Installing the package

Install the stable development version of the package with:

``` r

install.packages("forecast.vocs", repos = "https://epiforecasts.r-universe.dev")
```

Install the unstable development from GitHub using the following,

``` r

remotes::install_github("epiforecasts/forecast.vocs", dependencies = TRUE)
```

### Installing CmdStan

If you don’t already have CmdStan installed then, in addition to
installing `forecast.vocs`, it is also necessary to install CmdStan
using CmdStanR’s `install_cmdstan()` function to enable model fitting in
`forecast.vocs`. A suitable C++ toolchain is also required. Instructions
are provided in the [*Getting started with
CmdStanR*](https://mc-stan.org/cmdstanr/articles/cmdstanr.html)
vignette. See the [CmdStanR
documentation](https://mc-stan.org/cmdstanr/) for further details and
support.

``` r

cmdstanr::install_cmdstan()
```

## Quick start

This quick start uses data from Germany that includes COVID-19
notifications and sequences with sequences either being positive or
negative for the Delta variant. It shows how to produce forecasts for
both a one and two strain model for the 19th of June 2021 when the
latest available data estimated that approximately 7% of COVID-19 were
positive for the Delta variant. Note that estimated growth rates and
reproduction numbers shown here have been rescaled using an assumed
generation time of 5.5 days and a weakly informative prior centred
around Delta being 50% more transmissible than non-Delta cases has been
used.

``` r

library(forecast.vocs)
options(mc.cores = 4)

obs <- filter_by_availability(
  germany_covid19_delta_obs,
  date = as.Date("2021-06-19")
)
obs
#>           date location_name location  cases cases_available seq_total seq_voc
#>  1: 2021-03-20       Germany       DE  87328      2021-03-20        NA      NA
#>  2: 2021-03-27       Germany       DE 109442      2021-03-27        NA      NA
#>  3: 2021-04-03       Germany       DE 117965      2021-04-03        NA      NA
#>  4: 2021-04-10       Germany       DE 107223      2021-04-10        NA      NA
#>  5: 2021-04-17       Germany       DE 142664      2021-04-17      4072       6
#>  6: 2021-04-24       Germany       DE 145568      2021-04-24      4500      32
#>  7: 2021-05-01       Germany       DE 131887      2021-05-01      3607      55
#>  8: 2021-05-08       Germany       DE 107141      2021-05-08      4491      86
#>  9: 2021-05-15       Germany       DE  77261      2021-05-15      3443      92
#> 10: 2021-05-22       Germany       DE  57310      2021-05-22      3392     114
#> 11: 2021-05-29       Germany       DE  33052      2021-05-29      2258      89
#> 12: 2021-06-05       Germany       DE  22631      2021-06-05      1136      75
#> 13: 2021-06-12       Germany       DE  15553      2021-06-12        NA      NA
#> 14: 2021-06-19       Germany       DE   7659      2021-06-19        NA      NA
#>       share_voc seq_available
#>  1:          NA          <NA>
#>  2:          NA          <NA>
#>  3:          NA          <NA>
#>  4:          NA          <NA>
#>  5: 0.001473477    2021-06-16
#>  6: 0.007111111    2021-06-16
#>  7: 0.015248129    2021-06-16

#> 14:          NA    2021-07-29

current_obs <- latest_obs(germany_covid19_delta_obs)
```

### Forecast all-in-one

Run a forecast for both one and two strain models (or optionally just
one of these) using the
[`forecast()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/forecast.md)
function. This provides a wrapper around other package tooling to
initialise, fit, and summarise forecasts. Multiple forecasts can be
performed efficiently across dates and scenarios using
[`forecast_across_dates()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/forecast_across_dates.md)
and
[`forecast_across_scenarios()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/forecast_across_scenarios.md).

``` r

forecasts <- forecast(obs,
  strains = c(1, 2), voc_scale = c(0.4, 0.2),
  voc_label = "Delta", scale_r = 5.5 / 7,
  adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 15,
  refresh = 0, show_messages = FALSE
)
forecasts
#>    id forecast_date strains overdispersion variant_relationship  r_init
#> 1:  0    2021-06-19       1           TRUE           correlated 0, 0.25
#> 2:  0    2021-06-19       2           TRUE           correlated 0, 0.25
#>    voc_scale error               fit       data  fit_args samples max_rhat
#> 1:  0.4, 0.2       <CmdStanMCMC[42]> <list[28]> <list[5]>    4000        1
#> 2:  0.4, 0.2       <CmdStanMCMC[42]> <list[28]> <list[5]>    4000        1
#>    divergent_transitions per_divergent_transitions max_treedepth
#> 1:                     7                   0.00175             9
#> 2:                     9                   0.00225            10
#>    no_at_max_treedepth per_at_max_treedepth time              posterior
#> 1:                3693              0.92325 10.6 <fv_posterior[167x20]>
#> 2:                 500              0.12500 38.6 <fv_posterior[474x20]>
#>                 forecast
#> 1: <fv_posterior[12x13]>
#> 2: <fv_posterior[60x13]>
```

Summarised posterior and forecast estimates can be directly extracted
from the output using the included
[`summary()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/summary.html) method.
Alternatively, the complete summarised posterior can be extracted using
the following (which also has its own
[`summary()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/summary.html) and
[`plot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/plot.default.html) options to make
exploring the results easier). See the documentation for further
details.

``` r

summary(forecasts, target = "posterior", type = "all")
```

Plot the posterior prediction for cases from the single strain model
(“Overall”), from the two strain model (“Combined”), and the unobserved
estimates for each strain.

``` r

plot(forecasts, current_obs)
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-8-1.png)

Plot the posterior prediction for the fraction of cases that have the
Delta variant from the two strain model.

``` r

plot(forecasts, current_obs, type = "voc_frac", voc_label = "Delta variant")
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-9-1.png)

Plot the posterior estimate for the growth rate over the mean of the
generation time for COVID-19 cases (here assumed to be 5.5 days).

``` r

plot(forecasts, type = "growth")
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-10-1.png)

Plot the posterior estimate for the effective reproduction number of
Delta and non-Delta cases.

``` r

plot(forecasts, type = "rt")
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-11-1.png)

Plot the estimated transmission advantage for Delta vs non-Delta over
time. Note that as here a model with a correlated variant growth rates
has been used meaning that the difference between variants may vary over
time (potentially suitable where imports or present or a variant has
greater immune escape than the baseline). If it is likely that the
growth advantage is constant over time consider the fixed scaling model.
If the variants are likely to be circulating in independent populations
consider the independent variant model. See the documentation and model
definition vignette for details.

``` r

plot(forecasts, type = "voc_advantage")
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-12-1.png)

Alternatively a list of all plots with sensible defaults can be produced
using the following.

``` r

plot(forecasts, current_obs, type = "all", voc_label = "Delta variant")
```

A potentially useful optional integration with
[`scoringutils`](https://epiforecasts.io/scoringutils/) package is also
provided to streamline scoring forecasts using proper scoring rules. See
the documentation of the `scoringutils` package for more on this but as
a simple example below we calculate average scores both the single and
two strain models for this single Forecast

``` r

library(scoringutils)
library(knitr)

summary(forecasts, target = "forecast", type = "cases") |>
  fv_score_forecast(current_obs) |>
  summarise_scores(by = "strains") |>
  kable()
```

| strains | obs_overdispersion | obs_overdispersion | interval_score | dispersion | underprediction | overprediction | coverage_deviation | bias | ae_median |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 1 | 1 | 2056.375 | 277.750 | 1779.750 | 0 | -0.375 | NA | NA |
| 2 | 1 | 1 | 1118.750 | 507.125 | 610.875 | 0 | 0.000 | NA | NA |

### Step by step forecast

Rather than using the all-in-one
[`forecast()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/forecast.md)
function individual package functions can be used to produce a forecast
as follows.

``` r

dt <- fv_as_data_list(obs, horizon = 4)

model <- fv_model(strains = 2)

inits <- fv_inits(dt, strains = 2)

fit <- fv_sample(
  data = dt, model = model, init = inits,
  voc_scale = c(0.4, 0.2),
  adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 15,
  refresh = 0, show_messages = FALSE
)

posterior <- fv_tidy_posterior(fit, voc_label = "Delta", scale_r = 5.5 / 7)
```

As for forecasts produced with the
[`forecast()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/forecast.md)
function summary plots and estimates can then be produced using
[`summary()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/summary.html), and
[`plot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/plot.default.html) methods. For
example case forecasts can be returned using the following,

``` r

summary(posterior, type = "cases", forecast = TRUE)
```

If using `forecast.vocs` in your work please consider citing it using
the following,

``` R
#>
```

## How to make a bug report or feature request

Please briefly describe your problem and what output you expect in an
[issue](https://github.com/epiforecasts/forecast.vocs/issues). If you
have a question, please don’t open an issue. Instead, ask on our [Q and
A
page](https://github.com/epiforecasts/forecast.vocs/discussions/categories/q-a).

## Contributing

We welcome contributions and new contributors! We particularly
appreciate help on priority problems in the
[issues](https://github.com/epiforecasts/forecast.vocs/issues). Please
check and add to the issues, and/or add a [pull
request](https://github.com/epiforecasts/forecast.vocs/pulls).

## Code of Conduct

Please note that the `forecast.vocs` project is released with a
[Contributor Code of
Conduct](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).
By contributing to this project, you agree to abide by its terms.

# Package index

## Forecast

Functions for forecasting across models, dates, and scenarios.

- [`forecast()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/forecast.md) :
  Forecast using branching processes at a target date
- [`forecast_across_dates()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/forecast_across_dates.md)
  : Forecast across multiple dates
- [`forecast_across_scenarios()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/forecast_across_scenarios.md)
  : Forecast across multiple scenarios and dates
- [`forecast_n_strain()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/forecast_n_strain.md)
  : Forecast for a single model and summarise
- [`plot(`*`<fv_forecast>`*`)`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/plot.fv_forecast.md)
  : Plot method for forecast
- [`summary(`*`<fv_forecast>`*`)`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/summary.fv_forecast.md)
  : Summary method for forecast
- [`unnest_posterior()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/unnest_posterior.md)
  : Unnest posterior estimates from a forecast data.frame

## Model

Functions for fitting the forecasting models.

- [`fv_as_data_list()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/fv_as_data_list.md)
  : Format data for use with stan
- [`fv_inits()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/fv_inits.md) :
  Set up initial conditions for model
- [`fv_model()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/fv_model.md) :
  Load and compile a strain model
- [`fv_sample()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/fv_sample.md)
  : Fit a brancing process strain model

## Preprocess

Functions for preprocessing observations.

- [`filter_by_availability()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/filter_by_availability.md)
  : Filter data based on availability and forecast date
- [`fv_dow_period()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/fv_dow_period.md)
  : Calculate the day of the week periodicity
- [`latest_obs()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/latest_obs.md)
  : Filter for latest observations of all types
- [`piecewise_steps()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/piecewise_steps.md)
  : Calculate piecewise steps

## Postprocess

Functions for postprocessing model output.

- [`convert_to_stanfit()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/convert_to_stanfit.md)
  : Convert to stanfit object
- [`extract_draws()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/extract_draws.md)
  : Extract posterior draws
- [`extract_forecast_dates()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/extract_forecast_dates.md)
  : Extract forecast dates
- [`fv_extract_forecast()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/fv_extract_forecast.md)
  : Extract forecasts from a summarised posterior
- [`fv_posterior()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/fv_posterior.md)
  : Summarise the posterior
- [`fv_tidy_posterior()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/fv_tidy_posterior.md)
  : Summarise the posterior tidily
- [`link_dates_with_posterior()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/link_dates_with_posterior.md)
  : Link dates by time for posterior parameter estimates
- [`link_obs_with_posterior()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/link_obs_with_posterior.md)
  : Link posterior estimates with observed data
- [`plot(`*`<fv_posterior>`*`)`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/plot.fv_posterior.md)
  : Plot method for fv_tidy_posterior
- [`print(`*`<fv_posterior>`*`)`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/print.fv_posterior.md)
  : Print method for fv_tidy_posterior
- [`quantiles_to_long()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/quantiles_to_long.md)
  : Convert summarised quantiles from wide to long format
- [`summary(`*`<fv_posterior>`*`)`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/summary.fv_posterior.md)
  : Summary method for fv_tidy_posterior
- [`update_voc_label()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/update_voc_label.md)
  : Label the Variant of Concern

## Plot

Functions for plotting postprocessed forecast model output.

- [`add_forecast_dates()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/add_forecast_dates.md)
  : Add the forecast dates to a plot
- [`plot(`*`<fv_forecast>`*`)`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/plot.fv_forecast.md)
  : Plot method for forecast
- [`plot(`*`<fv_posterior>`*`)`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/plot.fv_posterior.md)
  : Plot method for fv_tidy_posterior
- [`plot_cases()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/plot_cases.md)
  : Plot the posterior prediction for cases
- [`plot_default()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/plot_default.md)
  : Default posterior plot
- [`plot_growth()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/plot_growth.md)
  : Plot the posterior prediction for the growth rate
- [`plot_pairs()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/plot_pairs.md)
  : Pairs plot of parameters of interest and fitting diagnostics
- [`plot_posterior()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/plot_posterior.md)
  : Plot posterior predictions
- [`plot_rt()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/plot_rt.md) :
  Plot the posterior prediction for the reproduction number
- [`plot_theme()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/plot_theme.md)
  : Add the default plot theme
- [`plot_voc_advantage()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/plot_voc_advantage.md)
  : Plot the posterior prediction for the transmission advantage for the
  variant of concern
- [`plot_voc_frac()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/plot_voc_frac.md)
  : Plot the population posterior prediction for the fraction of samples
  with the variant of concern
- [`save_plots()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/save_plots.md)
  : Save plots by name

## Model validation

Functions for validating model fits and forecasts.

- [`bp_launch_shinystan()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/bp_launch_shinystan.md)
  : Launch shinystan
- [`fv_score_forecast()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/fv_score_forecast.md)
  : Evaluate forecasts using proper scoring rules
- [`plot_pairs()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/plot_pairs.md)
  : Pairs plot of parameters of interest and fitting diagnostics

## Generate data

Functions for generating simulated data.

- [`generate_obs()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/generate_obs.md)
  : Generate Simulated Observations
- [`sample_sequences()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/sample_sequences.md)
  : Sample Sequence Observation Model

## Define and generate scenarios

Functions for defining and generating data scenarios.

- [`define_scenarios()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/define_scenarios.md)
  : Define data availability scenarios
- [`generate_obs_scenario()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/generate_obs_scenario.md)
  : Define observed data for a scenario
- [`update_obs_availability()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/update_obs_availability.md)
  : Update observations based on availability

## Datasets

Package datasets used in examples and by users to explore the package
functionality.

- [`fv_example()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/fv_example.md)
  : Load a package example
- [`germany_covid19_delta_obs`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/germany_covid19_delta_obs.md)
  : Test positive COVID-19 cases and sequences in Germany

## Check inputs

Functions to check the structure of user inputs.

- [`check_dataframe()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/check_dataframe.md)
  : Check a data.frame
- [`check_observations()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/check_observations.md)
  : Check observations are in the correct format
- [`check_param()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/check_param.md)
  : Check a parameter is the correct type and length
- [`check_quantiles()`](epiforecasts.io/forecast.vocs/reference/check_quantiles.md)
  : Check Quantiles Required are Present
